thesis: The model can interpret and propose; deterministic identity, scope, authority and effect boundaries decide what can happen.

evidence.claim: Capability authority is resolved outside model output.
Instruction provenance cannot grant effect authority.
Capabilities declare roles, risk and provider.
Protected scopes and malicious effect requests fail closed.
Production context rejects cross-tenant actors.
Persistence and object-store reference boundaries are tenant-scoped.
Write/external capabilities require approval.
Recorded approval identity can be bound to trust evidence.
Source, integrity, authority, exact evidence, derivation and decision form the common trust chain.
Trust-chain invariants are regression tested.
Secrets, credentials, system prompt, policy/audit mutation and cross-tenant scopes are protected.
Sensitive audit values are redacted.
Tool-call and subagent-depth ceilings fail closed.
Budget exhaustion and recursive-depth attacks are regression cases.
Security and trust decisions are attached to production audit events.
Effect queue records security/trust decision evidence.
Known-bad components are blocked and unverified components are surfaced for review.
Supply-chain attack states are covered in the shared gauntlet.
40 cross-domain adversarial cases cover OWASP Agentic Top 10 categories.
Security gauntlet is a CI release gate.
Runtime security denials and trust decisions are auditable.
Real incident response and production anomaly evidence remain explicit residual work.

residualRisks: Shared gauntlet proves deterministic boundary behavior, not live-model injection detection.
SBOM, signatures and complete dependency provenance are not yet part of this shared contract.
Production incident/anomaly monitoring needs real deployment evidence.
Domain adapters must add stricter legal, clinical, administrative or customer-specific release gates.
External security review is required before production-security claims.
